project: tour-travel-3d (Rahi Travels): Next.js 16 tour/cab site with a scroll-driven SVG road, a WebGL car and an admin CRM on MongoDB. Path /Users/amangupta/Desktop/FL/tour-travel-3d, branch main. Audited read-only on 2026-10-11.
summary: The backend half of tour-travel-3d is strong and mostly reusable as-is: the API envelope and error mapping (withRoute/AppError), the MongoDB fixed-window rate limiter, the silent-discard spam pipeline, jose+bcrypt sessions with tokenVersion revocation, capability RBAC, the Mongoose 9 model pattern, a $facet dashboard service, a URL-state admin list hook, an api-client with 401 bounce, two static audit scripts and a black-box smoke test. The front-end 3D system is the weak half, and the user's three complaints trace to specific code. (1) The car is too fast and not smooth because car-rider.tsx implements a 'drive law' of one page pixel per scroll pixel. It writes element.style.transform straight from a passive scroll listener, with no damping or speed cap. A smoothDamp(maxSpeed) helper exists in src/lib/motion/damp.ts but has zero call sites. Position also updates on the compositor while heading updates in a separate WebGL render gated by HEADING_EPSILON, so the two run at different cadences. (2) On mobile the road hugs the left because the road is a DOM-measured SVG that has to avoid content. Below 768px ('spine' mode) it is a 30px ribbon in a 36px gutter with about ±3px of weave, and the hero car is drawn at 0.55 opacity. (3) The 'drawing type' look comes from the 'totems' being flat SVG polygons (paper fill plus ink stroke). The 3D Clash-Royale-style totem spec in journey-art.md was never built. Process mistakes: the art direction changed three times in about a day (dark, then a 3D night journey, then flat light), leaving about 1,100 lines of dead journey code and roughly 5,000 lines of road-taper/excursion machinery that still has three open blockers. Briefs contradict each other on several points. The site also ships fabricated stats and testimonials. Web3Forms is called server-side, which its own docs say returns 403 unless you have a paid plan and a safelisted IP. A stale session cookie can plausibly cause a /admin ↔ /admin/login redirect loop. The user:manage capability is defined but no admin-management feature exists. .env.example and .agent-briefs are gitignored, and the whole v3 rebuild is uncommitted (81 changed files).
stack_versions: On disk in tour-travel-3d: next 16.4.0, react/react-dom 19.3.0 (R3F 9 peer range is >=19 <19.4, so do not bump React past 19.3 without re-checking), typescript ^5, tailwindcss 4.3.3 with @tailwindcss/turbopack 4.3.3 (no PostCSS, no tailwind.config), three 0.186.1 / @types/three 0.186.0, @react-three/fiber 9.8.1, @react-three/drei 10.7.9, motion 14.0.0 (re-exports framer-motion 14), mongoose 9.11.0 (driver mongodb 7.7, Node >=20.19), zod 4.6.5, react-hook-form 7.89.0, @hookform/resolvers 5.9.1, jose 6.2.12, bcryptjs 3.0.3, recharts 3.10.1, sonner 2.0.8, lucide-react 1.52.0, date-fns 4.4.0, tsx 4.23.15, mongodb-memory-server 11.3.0, eslint 9 with eslint-config-next 16.4.0 (flat config; `next lint` was removed). Dev server pinned to :3007, dev Mongo on :27018. ProDevly must re-verify every version against its own node_modules at install time. The briefs' rule is 'read node_modules/next/dist/docs, not memory'.
brief_digest: CONTRACT.md: CONTRACT overrides every other brief. Next16: src/proxy.ts (not middleware.ts); params/searchParams/cookies()/headers() are Promises, always await; error.tsx prop is `retry`, not `reset`; next/image uses `preload`, not `priority`; revalidateTag(tag, profile) takes two args; cacheComponents is OFF, so `export const dynamic`/`revalidate` are legal. Tailwind4: no tailwind.config, all tokens in globals.css; semantic token classes only (bg-surface-1, text-fg-muted, never bg-zinc-900); always write `border border-border` because the default border colour is currentColor; `ring` is 1px. Mongoose9: QueryFilter<T> replaces FilterQuery; type models via `declare module 'mongoose' { interface Models {...} }` (a `models.X as Model` cast is TS2352); sanitizeFilter is ON globally, so wrap EVERY self-authored operator in mongoose.trusted(), and setOptions({sanitizeFilter:false}) does NOT override it. Zod4: z.email(), `error:` instead of `message:`, error.issues. Conventions: @/ alias only; no barrel in components/ui; 'use client' only when state/effects/handlers are used; never return a raw Mongoose doc; build filters from parsed.data only; strict TS with no any, no @ts-ignore, no TODOs or placeholder copy; mobile-first checks at 360/390/768/1024/1440; tap targets ≥44px; run `tsc --noEmit` before returning.

next16.md: §0 cacheComponents:true removes dynamic/revalidate/dynamicParams, forces <Suspense> around every runtime read and breaks nonce CSP, so a DB-heavy app should set it false. Route handlers: `{ params }: { params: Promise<...> }`; GET is dynamic by default; runtime 'edge' is deprecated. Global PageProps/LayoutProps/RouteContext types exist only after `next typegen`, so CI runs `next typegen && tsc --noEmit`. Proxy: one exported function (`proxy` or default), Node runtime that cannot be configured, always set a negative matcher, no shared globals or DB in it, and re-check auth inside every Server Action. cookies().set only works in a Server Action or Route Handler. Caching (cacheComponents off): fetch is uncached by default, use unstable_cache for DB reads and connection() instead of unstable_noStore. Metadata: set metadataBase once in the root layout; OG/icon image functions receive params and id as Promises. next/image in 16: `preload` replaces `priority`; images.qualities defaults to [75] (list every quality you use); 16px dropped from imageSizes; minimumCacheTTL is 4h; remotePatterns replaces domains; localPatterns is needed for query strings. next/font: call at module scope and wire CSS vars through @theme inline. Server Actions: useActionState puts prevState first; redirect() goes outside try/catch. config: typedRoutes and cacheComponents are top-level keys; mongoose, mongodb and bcrypt are already auto-externalized (do not list them); lucide, date-fns and recharts are optimized by default. Breaking: every @slot needs a default.tsx; Turbopack is the default for dev and build (webpack config fails without --webpack); smooth scroll needs data-scroll-behavior='smooth' on <html>.

tailwind4.md: Wiring is turbopack.rules {'*.css': {loaders:['@tailwindcss/turbopack'], as:'*.css'}}. ZERO PostCSS: adding postcss.config is a regression, and so is `next build --webpack`, which drops Tailwind. Any CSS file that uses Tailwind at-rules must contain @import/@reference/@theme, or the loader silently skips it. Token namespaces decide the utilities generated (--color-*, --font-*, --text-* with --line-height, --radius-*, a single --spacing, --breakpoint-*, --container-*, --ease-*, --animate-*). THE key rule: theme switching via data-theme or data-ui requires `@theme inline { --color-bg: var(--bg) }`. A non-inline @theme freezes the :root value. Consequence: in hand-written CSS use var(--bg), not var(--color-bg). Declare keyframes inside @theme so they tree-shake. Opacity modifiers like bg-x/50 work on var tokens via color-mix, but bare channel lists (`30 144 255`) break; write every token as oklch()/hex. v3→v4 renames: shadow-sm→xs, rounded-sm→xs, outline-none vs outline-hidden (use outline-hidden for custom focus rings), bg-gradient→bg-linear; *-opacity-* utilities were removed. ring is 1px with a currentColor default; container has no centering or padding. Container queries are built in (@container, @md:). Use motion-safe:/motion-reduce: plus a global reduced-motion CSS backstop. No auto-detection of tailwind.config.

three-r3f.md: R3F v9 JSX typing augments module 'react' (never `declare global JSX`); prop types are ThreeElements['mesh']; extend() needs a ThreeElements augmentation. Use state.pointer (state.mouse is deprecated); renderer creation is async. Canvas defaults: SRGB output plus ACESFilmic. Use NeutralToneMapping for saturated paint, because ACES greys it out. A useFrame with priority >0 stops auto-render. three 0.186: physically-correct lights only (point/spot intensity in candela, decay=2); no outputEncoding or useLegacyLights; transmissionResolutionScale=0.5 for glass; keep opacity at 1 when transmission>0. drei 10: everything exists from the barrel; PresentationControls has no `config` prop; SoftShadows returns null. CRITICAL: <Environment preset> fetches HDRs from raw.githack.com at runtime. Use <Environment frames={1} resolution={256}> with <Lightformer> children instead (offline), or self-host files. Next integration: dynamic(..., {ssr:false}) only inside a 'use client' file; never import three from a server, route or layout file; transpilePackages and serverExternalPackages are not needed. Canvas already suspends, so add your own <Suspense> around useGLTF; self-host Draco with useGLTF.setDecoderPath('/draco/'). Perf: dpr [1,1.5]; PerformanceMonitor plus AdaptiveDpr can stomp each other; with frameloop 'demand' call invalidate() after every change; dispose anything created with `new` or useMemo; use <Instances> for more than ~50 copies; useDetectGPU tiers; reduced motion = no spin/float/parallax plus demand frameloop. Canvas `fallback` is NOT a loading state; the real poster is next/dynamic `loading` plus an image. The wrapper needs a real height before mount. Never read window or matchMedia during render. Handle webglcontextlost with preventDefault. (The poster snippet still uses deprecated `priority`, a contradiction.)

mongoose-zod.md: Mongoose 9 removed count(), update(), remove(), findOneAndRemove and callbacks; pre hooks are async with no next(); `new:true` is replaced by returnDocument:'after'; update pipelines need {updatePipeline:true}; isValidObjectId(123) is false. New: insertOne, and findAndCount (needs sort and limit). strictQuery is false by default, so set true. Typed schema pattern: Schema<Raw, Model, Methods, {}, Virtuals>; statics on the model interface; annotate `this`; subdocs as plain Schema with {_id:false}. Models augmentation avoids OverwriteModelError on HMR. Use schema.index() for compound, TTL (expireAfterSeconds:0 on a Date) and text indexes; 'background' was removed. autoIndex is ON by default, including production, so turn it off in prod and run syncIndexes()/diffIndexes from a script. aggregate<R> returns R[]; a $facet sub-array can be [], so use ?. everywhere; $match is NOT sanitized or cast. Transactions fail on a standalone mongod (code 20); design single-document atomicity or compare-and-swap, or use a replica set. Counter: findOneAndUpdate {upsert:true, returnDocument:'after'} without lean is the only non-null typing. Cached connection: bufferCommands:false, serverSelectionTimeoutMS 8000, maxPoolSize 10, never disconnect per request. sanitizeFilter throws on $where/$expr/$text, so $text needs trusted(). Zod 4: top-level z.email/url/uuid/iso.*; `error` param; .refine on an object keeps .shape; z.flattenError/treeifyError replace .flatten(); z.coerce input is `unknown`, so useForm<z.input<S>, unknown, z.output<S>> needs all three generics with zodResolver; z.stringbool for 'true'/'false'; z.enum(constArray); prefer z.strictObject for API bodies; optional text uses union [string, literal('').transform(undefined)]; keep one schema module shared by client and server.

seo-a11y-security.md: JSON-LD: a plain <script type=application/ld+json> with serializeJsonLd escaping < > & U+2028 U+2029; one @graph with stable @id values (#organization, #website); never duplicate NAP across nodes; no self-declared aggregateRating. sitemap/robots: lastModified must be the real updatedAt; generateSitemaps id is Promise<string>; staging robots disallow all; noindex the admin via metadata or X-Robots-Tag. Headers: pragmatic CSP (nonces are incompatible with static and PPR rendering); add 'wasm-unsafe-eval' plus worker-src/child-src blob: for Draco/KTX2; frame-ancestors 'none'; HSTS; nosniff; Permissions-Policy; COOP/CORP caveats; ship Report-Only first. Rate limit: Mongo fixed window keyed `bucket|key|windowStart` as _id with $inc plus $setOnInsert expiresAt and a TTL index; failClosed for auth, fail-open for leads; never inside proxy. Client IP: NextRequest.ip no longer exists; prefer x-vercel-forwarded-for; off Vercel take the RIGHTMOST XFF hop minus trusted hops (first-hop XFF is the classic bypass); collapse IPv6 to /64; never key on 'unknown'. Spam, no captcha, cheapest first: Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site → honeypot (offscreen, real-sounding name, return 200) → HMAC-signed time token (3s floor, 2h stale) → zod → content heuristics → IP/phone limits → dedupe window → persist. CSRF: Server Actions check Origin automatically, Route Handlers do NOT; reject sec-fetch-site cross-site AND same-site; never mutate on GET; 8h sessions with a __Host- cookie. A11y: skip link to <main tabIndex=-1>; one global :focus-visible ring ≥3:1; scroll-padding-top for a sticky header; native <dialog>.showModal() (no hand-rolled focus trap; guard if !open); useId-based aria-describedby hint+error, role=alert, noValidate, focus the first invalid field; badges carry icon+text+colour; the canvas is aria-hidden and all info is also in DOM. CWV: the canvas must never be the LCP (SSR an h1/poster); reserve the box with svh; no setState in useFrame; defer the canvas until idle AND in view, and skip it on saveData/2g/<4GB/reduced-motion; budget <1.5MB and <80k tris; draco+ktx2.

journey-architecture.md: Use a fixed `inset-0 -z-10` canvas behind native document scroll. drei ScrollControls loses: it hijacks scroll and kills SEO, sticky elements, anchors and find-in-page. Mount it from the page, never the layout, and never under an ancestor with transform/filter/contain. Drive it from one motion useScroll with trackContentSize:true (motion adds no ResizeObserver for the document). Keep a module-singleton state (no React state in the hot path) and a setWake/requestFrame slot so the scroll writer chunk never imports three. solve() gives each section an EQUAL share of progress regardless of pixel height. frameloop='demand': one pump useFrame at priority -1 damps a single value u, with idle motion from an external setInterval heartbeat (a self-throttling useFrame dies). Clamp dt to 1/30 everywhere; snap on hash/popstate/first frame/gap>0.08; never damp two values in series; never use a spring that overshoots (the car reverses). Undamped stage progress drives anything that must align with text. Legibility: a scene-veil ::before per section with a --veil opacity, opaque until data-journey='on'; ≥0.80 for sections with type under 14px; no backdrop-filter over the live canvas. Mobile URL bar: Canvas resize {scroll:false, debounce:{resize:200}}, stableViewportHeight() ignores height-only changes under 160px; rebuild the curve on width only. Add an admin-reachability audit so three never reaches /admin. Reduced motion: never import the scene. Content may never be gated on scroll progress.

journey-camera.md: Use one PerspectiveCamera with fov locked (29) and interpolate in orbit space (r, φ, θ along the shortest arc) instead of lerping Cartesian positions; the naive chord lerp gives a 2.3× size pump. Drive all channels from one smootherstep and don't stagger them. lerp(a,b,0.1) per frame depends on frame rate; MathUtils.damp is independent of it but lags in proportion to speed. Use a critically damped smoothDamp(state, target, smoothTime, dt, maxSpeed) instead: smoothTime of 0.38s for position, 0.22s for aim, 0.55s for azimuth. Cap yaw with maxSpeed (50°/s while driving, 150°/s for a deliberate move) and clamp lag to ±55°. Take heading from a chord (8m behind, 16m ahead), not the instantaneous tangent. Look ahead about 22m and bias 0.75 so the subject sits in the lower third. getPointAt (arc-length) rather than getPoint; arcLengthDivisions about 2000; clamp u to [0,1] (getPointAt(-ε) throws). Keep the subject out of the text with camera.setViewOffset, not by moving the subject. Never let φ reach 0 and never roll.

journey-performance.md: Triangles don't kill a page-long scene; these four things do: MeshReflectorMaterial past the hero, a real shadow map, shader programs compiling mid-scroll, and scroll position in React state. Desktop budget: ≤11ms frame, ≤45 draw calls, ≤120k tris, ≤14 programs, flat geometry memory, ≤24MB textures, dpr [1,1.5]. Merge multi-mesh hero objects per material (24→5 calls). Instance props with one shared material object (instancingColor is a define, so a mismatch means two programs). Preload must cover every prop kind (mount one of each for frame 0). Lambert with flatShading for props and Standard only for hero objects; no Toon. Use blob shadows rather than a shadow map, and ContactShadows only under the hero. Window props along the path. Keep one WebGL context; handle webglcontextrestored by remounting via key; pause rather than unmount. A PerformanceMonitor step ladder (dpr 1.5→1.25→1.0→cut density); drop AdaptiveDpr. Measure with gl.info, not Stats, on a 2019 integrated-GPU laptop. Its mobile decision was to NOT run the scene below 768px, which is the root of the mobile problem (see mistakes).

journey-road.md and journey-art.md: Path: CatmullRomCurve3 centripetal (tension is ignored except for 'catmullrom'); minimum-radius constraint; lead-in/out points; getPointAt plus arcLengthDivisions; a ribbon mesh built from a fixed world-up basis (computeFrenetFrames flips); uv.y in metres; an onBeforeCompile material with customProgramCacheKey; a shader dissolve on arc length for road emergence. Art (journey-art §3, the 3D totem rules worth reusing for ProDevly): base-heavy proportion; readable as a black silhouette at 48px; at most three volumes; flat shading with low radial segments (cones 7, cylinders 6, icosahedron detail 0–1); ONE consistent bevel across the set (RoundedBox radius 0.06); exaggerated scale of 1.3–1.8×; one lit face per prop; zero textures, variation via <Instance color> within ±6% lightness; no Outlines or Edges; nothing animated except the hero object; ≤160 props visible, ≤9 draw calls per zone. Do NOT reuse its chroma rules (night palette, ≤20% saturation, 'no green tree'): they contradict ProDevly's colourful brief.

art-direction.md, flat-art-direction.md, flat-road-system.md, flat-car.md: These are superseded design laws. Reusable anti-pattern list (§8): no purple/blue SaaS gradient with a glass card; glass in one place only; no icons in coloured circles; no emoji; no rounded-everything; testimonials without stars or avatars carousels; count-ups fire once; no AI-stock hero photography; no trust ribbons; ≤3 weights per viewport; no default ease. House easing tokens (--ease-out-expo cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) and others). Motion: only animate transform/opacity/filter/clip-path/stroke-dashoffset; hovers ≤240ms; entrances ≥400ms. Admin CRM spec (§9): 13px base, 44/52px rows, no zebra or vertical rules, right-aligned mono numerics, 22px status chips with a dot, 256px sidebar collapsing to a 56px rail, recharts with horizontal grid only and a near-black primary series, isAnimationActive=false on filtered charts, no motion beyond state feedback. flat-art-direction's 'colourful' idea: colour belongs to the page (full-bleed washes) with paper cards, chroma wide and lightness narrow (washes within about 1 L* point), no #FFFFFF, red as a ≤2% signal. flat-road-system: one page-pixel SVG with anchors measured from the DOM (this is the design that failed on mobile). imagery.md and imagery.data.ts list verified Unsplash URLs; not relevant to ProDevly (no stock imagery).

reusable.what: withRoute(handler) wrapper and toErrorResponse(): maps AppError, ZodError (422 with field map), DatabaseUnavailableError (503), Mongo E11000 (409 with field) and Mongoose ValidationError into a single envelope `{ok:true,data}` / `{ok:false,error:{code,message,fields}}`. Unknown errors are logged server-side and answered with a generic 500. Error factories: badRequest, validationFailed, unauthorized, forbidden, notFound, conflict, rateLimited (sets Retry-After), serviceUnavailable.
reusable.reuse_how: Copy verbatim into ProDevly src/lib/api/. Add ErrorCode values for ProDevly ('LAST_SUPERADMIN', 'SELF_DELETE', 'PAYMENT_EXCEEDS_DUE'). Every route handler is `export const POST = withRoute(async (req, ctx) => {...})`. Rewrite the service-specific copy in the 503 message.

Validate with the same passwordSchema and keep it idempotent. For dev-db, consider MongoMemoryReplSet so payment+ledger writes can use transactions locally.

reusable.what: Dashboard in ONE $facet aggregation (total, byStatus, windows today/week/month, trend, breakdowns, recent) with typed StatsFacets and IST-day boundaries computed server-side ($match built from Dates only, since it is not sanitized).
reusable.reuse_how: Template for each ProDevly section dashboard (clients, projects, tasks, payments, vendors, expenses, team): one $facet per screen, emptyStatusCounts() defaults so zero rows render as 0, IST helpers from src/lib/utils/datetime.ts. Revenue vs expense vs vendor cost per project comes from a $lookup or separate facets keyed on projectId.

reusable.what: A DTO layer: every route returns serialize*(doc), never a raw Mongoose doc (ObjectId and Date are not JSON-safe).
reusable.reuse_how: Same layer for ProDevly DTOs. Never serialize passwordHash or payout bank details.

reusable.what: api-client unwraps the envelope into data or a thrown ApiClientError (code, status, fields, retryAfterSeconds) and hard-reloads to /admin/login?next= on 401 (on401:'throw' for the login form). use-admin-list keeps page/pageSize/search/sort/filters in the URL with router.replace and a debounced search, and never writes defaults to the URL. admin-nav is a capability-gated nav map with visibleAdminNav(role), isActiveAdminHref and adminPageTitle; icons are imported as components so they tree-shake.
reusable.reuse_how: Copy all three. Rebuild ADMIN_NAV groups for ProDevly: Overview (Dashboard), Clients (Clients, Projects, Tasks), Money (Client Payments, Third parties, Vendor Payments, Expenses), Team (Members & roles, Payouts), Account (Settings, Audit log).

reusable.path: src/components/ui/* (dialog, drawer, confirm-dialog, field, table, pagination, status-badge, toast, …) + src/components/admin/*
reusable.what: Design-system primitives per CONTRACT §4: native <dialog>.showModal() modals and drawers, Field a11y wiring, Table/TH sortable, StatusBadge with dot+text, a sonner Toaster wrapper. Admin shell: sidebar, topbar, user menu, page-header, data-toolbar, stat-tile, recharts trend chart.
reusable.reuse_how: Port the primitives and restyle the tokens for the ProDevly CRM. Keep the native-dialog approach and the CRM density spec (art-direction §9). Admin components that are booking-specific (calendar, plate) are reference only.

reusable.what: A notifier registry (Notifier interface, dispatch via Promise.allSettled, never throws into the request). Web3Forms transport with an 8s AbortSignal.timeout, `replyto` lowercase, botcheck:false; a console notifier in dev.
reusable.reuse_how: Keep the notifier registry and the fail-quiet rule, but move the Web3Forms call to the BROWSER (see mistakes): the client form POSTs to api.web3forms.com with the public access key, and in parallel to /api/leads to persist to Mongo. Run any server-side notifier inside `after()` from next/server rather than awaiting it in the response path.

reusable.what: Security headers (pragmatic CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, XFO DENY, Permissions-Policy with payment=()), no-store on /admin and /api, poweredByHeader false, cacheComponents false, turbopack Tailwind rule, optimizePackageImports for three/drei/fiber/motion, images formats avif/webp with explicit qualities.
reusable.reuse_how: Copy. For ProDevly add 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to script-src and blob: to worker-src/child-src (Draco/KTX2 GLB totems), connect-src https://api.web3forms.com (plus hCaptcha hosts if used), and form-action for Web3Forms. Remove the Unsplash and Google Maps entries unless they are used.

reusable.what: Pure-math smoothDamp(state, target, smoothTime, dt, maxSpeed) critically damped spring with overshoot guard, smoothDampAngle, wrapAngle, and band() (C2 smootherstep). No three import.
reusable.reuse_how: THE fix for 'car too fast': copy into ProDevly and actually use it. Scroll writes a target; a rAF or useFrame follower calls smoothDamp with smoothTime ≈0.35–0.6s and a maxSpeed in world units/s, with dt clamped to 1/30, and snaps on hash jumps.

reusable.what: useDeviceTier() returns 'low' on SSR and the first render, then measures (cores, deviceMemory, coarse pointer, a memoised WebGL2 probe that releases its context via WEBGL_lose_context). usePrefersReducedMotion. useMediaQuery via useSyncExternalStore with a false server snapshot.
reusable.reuse_how: Reuse the probe and the SSR-safe hooks, but change the policy: a phone should NOT be auto-'low'. Use tiers to choose quality (dpr, instance counts, shadow type, post-processing), not to remove the 3D experience on mobile.

reusable.what: A three-free scroll measurement singleton: section boxes measured on ResizeObserver(body), useScroll({trackContentSize:true}), and solve() that gives every section an equal share of progress. Snap flags on hashchange and popstate. It is dead code in this repo but is the right architecture.
reusable.reuse_how: Lift it into ProDevly as the scroll→scene driver for the fixed 3D canvas: section ids = navbar/hero/partners/projects/services/pricing/developers/contact. Pair it with the stableViewportHeight() snippet from journey-architecture §5.

reusable.what: JsonLd component, schema builders (with a deliberate 'no aggregateRating' note), pageMetadata() helper, and Next 16 metadata route files.
reusable.reuse_how: Reuse with Organization/ProfessionalService/WebSite nodes for ProDevly. Emit the site-wide graph only once (see the duplicate JSON-LD mistake). Use the hardened serializeJsonLd escaping.

reusable.what: Semantic tokens on :root, with [data-ui='light'] and [data-ui='dark'] overrides mapped through @theme inline; @custom-variant light; custom utilities (container-page, type-*, tabular, bleed, mask-edges, no-scrollbar); a reduced-motion backstop. next/font with Archivo (variable wdth axis), Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono as CSS variables.
reusable.reuse_how: Reuse the mechanism (tokens, @theme inline, data-ui scoping so the admin and marketing site share one CSS). Do not reuse the palette or fonts, which ProDevly must choose fresh. Never name a custom class or utility after a core Tailwind utility (overline collision).

mistakes.issue: The car is too fast to follow and feels mechanically glued to the scrollbar, because its position is a pure function of scrollY.
mistakes.evidence: src/components/car/car-rider.tsx 'THE DRIVE LAW': `y = park + scrollY` ('ONE PAGE PIXEL OF ROAD PER PIXEL OF SCROLL'). It is written synchronously in `window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true })` → write() → `element.style.transform = translate3d(...)`. src/lib/motion/damp.ts exports smoothDamp(…, maxSpeed) but `grep -rn smoothDamp src` finds no caller outside damp.ts. The LAMBDA=9 damp in journey-pump (journey-architecture §3) was deleted with the 3D world.
mistakes.root_cause: A client note ('car scroll k saath move nhi kr rhi') was over-corrected into hard 1:1 coupling. The follower/damping layer was dropped during the flat rebuild, and the comfort cap that journey-camera §3.4 specified was never wired.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Scroll only ever sets a TARGET. Every moving hero object or camera is a follower updated per frame in rAF/useFrame with smoothDamp(smoothTime 0.35–0.6s, maxSpeed in units/s), dt clamped to 1/30, and snap on hashchange/popstate/first frame/large jumps. Never write transforms from a scroll event. Map scroll to progress per section (equal share via solve()), not per pixel.

mistakes.issue: Car motion isn't smooth: position and rotation update on different clocks, and the canvas buffer resizes in steps.
mistakes.evidence: car-rider.tsx moves the DOM element on the compositor at scroll-event cadence, while heading is a WebGL re-render requested only when |Δrot| > HEADING_EPSILON=0.006 (car-state.ts) under frameloop='demand'. The 'buffer ladder' (bufferIndexFor/setBuffer) reallocates the canvas, and comments admit about 'eight visible pops' per read. A 30Hz setInterval heartbeat drives the idle animation. HANDOVER: scroll dispatch coalesces, so the car 'steps'.
mistakes.root_cause: A hybrid architecture (a small transparent WebGL canvas translated as a DOM element over an SVG road) was chosen to save fill-rate. Position, heading, scale and rendering live in four separate update paths.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: One renderer, one clock: a single fixed full-viewport R3F canvas where every transform (position, rotation, scale, camera) is derived in the same useFrame from the same damped state. No DOM-translated canvases, no threshold-gated renders for continuous motion, no canvas resizing during scroll. Use frameloop 'always' while the hero is in view (pause offscreen or when the tab is hidden), or 'demand' with a pump that invalidates until the spring settles.

mistakes.issue: Mobile view is monotonous: the road is a thin ribbon stuck in the left gutter and the car is a ghost.
mistakes.evidence: src/components/road/road-layer.tsx spine mode (<768px, measure-anchors.ts MODE_BREAKPOINTS): 'A 30px ribbon in a 36px gutter leaves the weave about ±3px of travel'. SPINE_CONTENT_INSET=36. car-metrics.ts CAR_HERO_OPACITY.spine=0.55. HANDOVER blockers #3–#5: excursion ladder inverted at 768, hero road funnels to 0.144 of its width, closing bookend missing below lg. journey-performance §7: 'The journey does not run below 768px… The composition does not exist at 390px.'
mistakes.root_cause: Mobile was treated as a degraded fallback of a desktop two-column composition (the road threads the 'empty column'). With no empty column on a phone, the scene was squeezed into a gutter. The road was also measured from DOM anchors, so content always wins and the art loses.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Design the phone composition first and separately. The 3D scene gets its own full-bleed moments: totems centre-stage between text blocks, camera choreography for portrait aspect, text over a scene-veil. It is never a strip beside content. Quality tiers change dpr, instance counts and effects, never whether the experience exists. Acceptance gate: review 390×844 and 360×800 screenshots before desktop polish.

mistakes.issue: The 'totems' are flat line drawings, not 3D objects (what the user called 'drawing type').
mistakes.evidence: src/components/totems/totem.tsx docblock: 'One slot's worth of roadside, as a single <svg>… the props become light line drawings on dark'. src/components/totems/shapes/desert.tsx draws KHEJRI as `<polygon … fill={TONE.paper} stroke={TONE.ink}>`. The real 3D totem spec (journey-art.md §3: 14 props, flat-shaded cones and icosahedra, RoundedBox bevel 0.06) was never built.
mistakes.root_cause: The pivot from the 3D world to a flat SVG system (flat-road-system.md, flat-car.md: 'demolition of the abandoned 3D world') turned every prop into SVG to fit the DOM-measured overlay.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Totems are real 3D meshes: modelled primitives or authored GLB (Draco/KTX2, self-hosted), lit with an offline Lightformer Environment and NeutralToneMapping so saturated colours survive. Keep journey-art §3 form rules (base-heavy, ≤3 volumes, consistent bevel, readable at 48px, one shared material per kind, instancing). Drop its grey/night chroma limits.

mistakes.issue: The art direction pivoted three times in about 24 hours, leaving dead code and an unfinished product.
mistakes.evidence: art-direction.md (dark, Oct 7) → journey-*.md (3D night drive, Oct 8 13:35) → flat-*.md (light colourful SVG, Oct 8 16:17). src/components/journey/* (~1,160 lines: journey-host, journey-scroll-writer, journey-stages, journey-state, route-line) is imported only by itself. app/(site)/page.tsx comment 'THE DELETED MOUNT'. HANDOVER: 'Not shippable yet', 3 blockers, '~80 changed files… uncommitted'.
mistakes.root_cause: The aesthetic was decided by writing long engineering specs instead of showing the client visual prototypes first. Each direction change was absorbed by agents rather than validated.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Lock the visual direction with the user BEFORE engineering: an artifact with 2–3 rendered options (stills and an interactive prototype at both desktop and 390px), then an explicit sign-off. After a pivot, delete superseded modules in the same change. Commit at every milestone on a branch.

mistakes.issue: Massive over-engineering of the road system, with blockers still open.
mistakes.evidence: src/components/road: road-taper.ts 1,145 lines, build-road.ts 812, road-layer.tsx 761, excursion-plan.ts 511, audit-crossings.ts 417. car-rider.tsx 668. HANDOVER blocker #1: the parked car overhangs the road at 1.45× because the rotated footprint was 'measured on the wrong axis' through three review rounds. An agent was mid-edit on excursion-plan.ts when the run stopped.
mistakes.root_cause: Binding a decorative scene to measured DOM geometry creates a combinatorial constraint system (every breakpoint × every section × the taper × the car size). Essay-length comments substituted for visual verification.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Decouple the 3D world from DOM layout. The scene has its own world coordinates and authored camera keyframes per section; DOM sections reserve designed safe zones (CSS) rather than having the scene measure them. Cap any single visual-system module at about 300 lines. Verify with screenshots at fixed scroll positions, not with numeric probes alone.

mistakes.issue: Fabricated statistics and testimonials are shipped on the public site.
mistakes.evidence: src/data/editorial.ts TRUST_STATS: trips 12,480+, cities 38, rating 4.9/5 — rendered by src/components/hero/hero-stats.tsx and src/components/sections/stats-band.tsx. src/data/testimonials.ts holds six invented named customers (e.g. 'Anuradha Menon').
mistakes.root_cause: Placeholder social proof was authored as 'real-sounding' copy, with no flag that it is fabricated.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: The user's rule is hard: no invented numbers, ratings, client counts or testimonials anywhere on the frontend. Use only verifiable facts (services offered, tech stack, process steps, real project names and partners supplied by the team). Where data is pending, render the section from the CMS/DB and hide it when empty. No placeholder figures. Add a grep check in verify for patterns like /\d+\+|\d+(\.\d)?\/5|\d+%/ in src/data and src/components/sections.

mistakes.issue: Web3Forms is called from the server, which Web3Forms rejects (403) unless you have a paid plan and a safelisted IP. Failures are swallowed, so notifications silently never arrive.
mistakes.evidence: src/services/web3forms.ts POSTs to https://api.web3forms.com/submit from the Node route path, returns false and console.errors on non-OK. docs.web3forms.com/getting-started/troubleshooting ('403: This method is not allowed'): the API 'is expected to run on client side'; server use requires adding the server IP to the Safelist and an active Paid subscription.
mistakes.root_cause: The access key was treated as a server secret (the comment says it must 'stay server-side'). The provider's client-side model was not verified.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Submit Web3Forms from the browser with the (public-by-design) access key restricted to the ProDevly domain in the Web3Forms dashboard, and add its host to CSP connect-src and form-action. In parallel, POST the same payload to /api/leads, which validates, spam-screens, rate-limits and persists to MongoDB as the system of record. Use server-side Web3Forms only on a paid plan with the server IP safelisted.

mistakes.issue: Email notification is awaited inside the response path, so a slow relay delays the user up to 8s.
mistakes.evidence: src/services/enquiry.service.ts:88 `await notifyNewEnquiry(enquiry)`. src/app/api/bookings/route.ts:147 `await notifyNewBooking(booking)`. web3forms.ts TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000.
mistakes.root_cause: Fail-quiet was implemented with try/catch, but the work was not moved off the request path.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Run post-response side effects (notifications, audit fan-out, cache revalidation pings) with `after()` from next/server. Respond as soon as Mongo acknowledges the write.

mistakes.issue: Plausible infinite redirect loop between /admin and /admin/login when a cookie is present but invalid.
mistakes.evidence: src/proxy.ts: `hasSession = Boolean(request.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE)?.value)`; `if (isLoginPage && hasSession) redirect('/admin')`. src/app/admin/(workspace)/layout.tsx: requireAdminPage() → redirect('/admin/login') when getCurrentAdmin() is null (revoked tokenVersion via password/route.ts `$inc: { tokenVersion: 1 }` on another device, a deactivated account, or a rotated AUTH_SECRET). The cookie lives 7 days. Not runtime-verified.
mistakes.root_cause: The proxy decides on cookie PRESENCE while the guard decides on cookie VALIDITY. Two layers with different truths redirect toward each other.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: The proxy verifies the JWT with jose before any redirect, and never bounces away from /admin/login on presence alone. When the guard finds an invalid session it redirects to a route handler that clears the cookie and then sends the user to login. Add a smoke test: revoke the token, then GET /admin and expect a single redirect to login.

mistakes.issue: Admin management is missing even though a capability exists for it; there is no per-admin activity trail.
mistakes.evidence: 'user:manage' appears in config/constants.ts:257 and only in comments elsewhere (password/route.ts:25, change-password-form.tsx:25). No /api/admin/users or admins route. Only a denormalised byName exists on booking statusHistory (models/booking.model.ts).
mistakes.root_cause: Scope stopped at a single seeded owner. Team management was deferred and never built.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Build these from day one: the Team/Admins module (superadmin-only create/update/delete/role change; cannot delete self; cannot remove or demote the last SUPER_ADMIN; delete = deactivate plus tokenVersion bump), and an AuditLog collection written by a single helper in every mutating service (actorId, actorName, action, entity, entityId, before/after diff, ip, at). This powers 'track their work and payments given to them'.

mistakes.issue: The rate limiter keys on a spoofable IP off Vercel.
mistakes.evidence: src/lib/api/request.ts clientIp(): falls back to `forwarded.split(',')[0]` (the first XFF hop). scripts/smoke.ts sets `'x-forwarded-for': RUN_IP` (TEST-NET-3) to get a fresh quota each run, which proves a client can choose its own key. seo-a11y-security.md §5b explicitly warned that the first hop is 'the single most common rate-limiter bypass'.
mistakes.root_cause: The brief's getClientIp (rightmost minus trusted hops, /64 IPv6 collapse) was simplified during implementation.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Use the brief's getClientIp(headers): prefer x-vercel-forwarded-for; otherwise rightmost XFF minus TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS; normalise and collapse IPv6 to /64; give 'unknown' a tight bucket. Tests reset limits through a script, not header spoofing.

mistakes.issue: Login lockout counter is a non-atomic read-modify-write, and the admin login limiter fails open.
mistakes.evidence: src/app/api/admin/auth/login/route.ts: `const failures = (admin.failedLoginAttempts ?? 0) + 1; await Admin.updateOne(..., { $set: { failedLoginAttempts: failures } })`. rate-limit.ts checkRateLimit catch → `{ allowed: true }` for every bucket including adminLogin, against seo brief §5a which says failClosed for auth.
mistakes.root_cause: Concurrency was not considered, and one fail-open policy was applied to all buckets.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: `$inc` with returnDocument:'after' for counters; set lockedUntil based on the returned value. Add a failClosed flag per rate-limit rule: auth, admin create and payments fail closed; the public lead form fails open.

mistakes.issue: The admin session is long-lived and the cookie is not hardened as the brief specified.
mistakes.evidence: src/lib/auth/session.ts SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 7 days, cookie 'tt_admin_session'. seo-a11y-security.md §7 recommends 8h plus the __Host- prefix.
mistakes.root_cause: Convenience over the brief's guidance.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: An admin panel handling client payments and payouts uses 8–12h sessions (optionally sliding), a `__Host-` cookie name in production (secure, path=/, no Domain), and tokenVersion revocation on role, password or status change.

mistakes.issue: Production indexes are never guaranteed: autoIndex is off in prod and there is no index-sync script.
mistakes.evidence: src/lib/db/mongoose.ts `mongoose.set('autoIndex', process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production')`; `grep -rn syncIndexes scripts src` returns nothing. The RateLimit TTL index and the Admin email unique index depend on it.
mistakes.root_cause: The brief's 'run syncIndexes() from a one-off script' (mongoose-zod §3.2) was not implemented.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Ship `npm run db:indexes` (tsx script calling Model.diffIndexes() then syncIndexes() for every model) and run it in the deploy pipeline before traffic.

mistakes.issue: The briefs contradict each other and the code, so agents could copy the wrong API.
mistakes.evidence: three-r3f.md §9 and seo-a11y-security.md §9.1 use `<Image … priority>` while next16.md §7 says priority is deprecated (use preload). mongoose-zod.md §8.2(b) says `.setOptions({ sanitizeFilter: false })` works, but CONTRACT.md and src/lib/db/mongoose.ts say it does NOT. seo-a11y-security.md §5a uses `mongoose.models.RateLimit as Model<…>`, which mongoose-zod §2.4 says is TS2352. Several briefs assume cacheComponents:true (`'use cache'` in sitemap) while CONTRACT sets it false.
mistakes.root_cause: Briefs were researched in parallel against an evolving config, with no reconciliation pass. CONTRACT patched only some conflicts.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Keep one CONTRACT.md that explicitly overrides everything. Before handing briefs to agents, run a contradiction pass (grep for priority, setOptions sanitizeFilter, `as Model`, `use cache`) and fix the briefs themselves, not just the contract.

mistakes.issue: The site-wide JSON-LD graph is emitted twice on the home page.
mistakes.evidence: src/app/(site)/layout.tsx `<JsonLd data={[buildOrganization(), buildTravelAgency(), buildWebSite()]} />` AND src/app/(site)/page.tsx `<JsonLd data={[buildOrganization(), buildTravelAgency(), buildWebSite(), buildTaxiService()]} />`.
mistakes.root_cause: The layout and page each added 'their' graph without a single owner.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Site-wide nodes are emitted only in the layout; pages add only page-specific nodes, linked by @id.

mistakes.issue: A custom class collides with a core Tailwind v4 utility.
mistakes.evidence: src/components/hero/hero-stats.tsx NOTE: Tailwind v4's core `overline` (text-decoration-line) plus an `@utility overline` in globals.css 'emits BOTH and the core rule lands last', drawing a literal overline. globals.css:711 works around it with an unlayered `.overline` rule.
mistakes.root_cause: Utility names were chosen without checking v4's core utility list.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Never name an @utility or a global class after a core Tailwind utility (overline, container, truncate, ring, shadow…). Prefix house utilities (e.g. `pd-eyebrow`).

mistakes.issue: Repo hygiene: the env template and the hard-won briefs are not versioned, the big rebuild is uncommitted, and the port is configured three ways.
mistakes.evidence: .gitignore has `.env*` (which also ignores .env.example; `git ls-files` shows none) and `/.agent-briefs/`. `git status --porcelain | wc -l` = 81; HANDOVER says 'Nothing is on a branch'. package.json `next dev -p 3007`, .claude/launch.json port 3000, .env NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=http://localhost:3000 (HANDOVER #8). HANDOVER also notes the Atlas password was pasted in chat.
mistakes.root_cause: Create-next-app defaults were left in place. Agent notes were treated as scratch. No commit discipline.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Use `.env*` plus `!.env.example` in .gitignore. Keep briefs under docs/briefs/ (committed). Define the port once (package.json) and derive launch.json and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL from it. Commit per milestone on a feature branch. Never paste secrets in chat, and generate AUTH_SECRET and FORM_TOKEN_SECRET with openssl.

mistakes.issue: The spam timing check uses an unsigned client timestamp.
mistakes.evidence: src/lib/api/spam.ts SpamCandidate.formLoadedAt: 'It is the client's own clock and is therefore forgeable… Making it unforgeable needs an HMAC token… see the note in the handover.'
mistakes.root_cause: The shared schema change for an HMAC token was deferred.
mistakes.rule_for_prodevly: Issue an HMAC-signed form token server-side (render it via a dynamic boundary or a tiny GET /api/form-token) and verify it with timingSafeEqual: under 3s is a silent discard, over 2h asks the user to refresh.

good_ideas: Two-layer auth: the proxy is a UX redirect only, and real authorisation (DB check of active and tokenVersion) runs in every route handler, page and Server Action via requireCapability/requireAdminPage.
tokenVersion in the JWT gives stateless sessions real revocation (password change kills all other sessions and reissues the current browser's cookie).
Timing-equalised login: fakeVerify() for unknown or locked accounts, an identical rejection message, two rate-limit buckets (IP and email) plus per-account lockout.
Capability-based RBAC with a capability-gated nav (visibleAdminNav). The UI hides what a role can't use, but the API check is what counts.
Silent-discard spam handling: a bot gets a decoy 200 response and nothing is persisted, so operators get no gradient. Content-Length is checked before the body is buffered.
Single API envelope plus a client api-client that unwraps it, throws ApiClientError carrying field errors for react-hook-form setError, and hard-reloads to login with ?next= on 401.
Admin list state lives in the URL (page/sort/filters/search via router.replace, defaults omitted), so views are shareable and refresh-safe.
One $facet aggregation per dashboard, so all numbers come from one consistent snapshot in one round-trip. Business-timezone day boundaries are computed server-side.

Immutable 'request snapshot' on the booking (original submission kept frozen next to the live, editable fields). For ProDevly, snapshot a project's agreed scope, budget and deadline at creation so changes are visible.
Atomic Counter.nextSequence for human-readable IDs (e.g. PDV-INV-2026-0001, PDV-PRJ-0042); the seed pushes counters past seeded IDs.
Denormalised actor on history entries (statusHistory[].byName plus id) so audit views render without joins and survive user deletion.
Static safety audits in `npm run verify`: un-trusted Mongo operators, and client components reaching the DB or auth. Add the inverse rule: the admin must not reach three.
Black-box smoke test against a running server with a cookie jar, covering the security-relevant behaviours (decoys, illegal transitions, logout, every admin screen renders).
Idempotent, deterministic seed (mulberry32 PRNG). It validates the seeded password against the live policy before connecting, refuses placeholder secrets in production and masks the URI in logs.
Zero-install dev MongoDB via mongodb-memory-server on a non-default port with persisted data (use MongoMemoryReplSet if payments need transactions).
Fixed full-viewport canvas behind native document scroll (not ScrollControls), mounted from the page, never from the layout; nothing above it with transform/filter/contain.
Three-free scroll writer plus a module singleton plus a setWake/requestFrame slot, so scroll measurement never pulls three into the main chunk and React never re-renders at scroll rate.
solve(): each section gets an equal share of scene progress regardless of its pixel height, so short sections don't get teleported past.
Undamped section progress for anything that must line up with text, and one damped value for moving objects (never damp in series).

scene-veil utility: a per-section ::before at a --veil opacity over the live canvas. It is opaque by default, so no-JS, no-WebGL and reduced-motion users get a fully legible page. Use ≥0.8 where type is under 14px.

stableViewportHeight() plus Canvas resize {scroll:false, debounce:{resize:200}} to absorb mobile URL-bar jitter. Rebuild width-dependent geometry on width only. Use offsetSize:true when the canvas wrapper is transformed.
Under frameloop='demand', idle motion needs an external heartbeat (setInterval), because a self-throttling useFrame stops being called. Clamp delta to 1/30 in every useFrame.

Offline lighting: drei <Environment frames={1} resolution={256}> with <Lightformer> children (no raw.githack HDR fetch). NeutralToneMapping keeps saturated colours from greying out, which matters for colourful totems.

One WebGL context for the whole site: a memoised WebGL2 probe that releases its test context, webglcontextlost preventDefault plus webglcontextrestored remount, and pausing (not unmounting) when offscreen or the tab is hidden.

SSR'd still (poster or SVG) is the LCP element, and the live canvas cross-fades in only after its first real frame (setCarLive/subscribeCarLive pattern). A server-rendered CSS arrival animation is mirrored by the canvas so the handover is seamless.
SSR-safe capability hooks: useMediaQuery via useSyncExternalStore with a false server snapshot; useDeviceTier returns 'low' on the server and first render, then upgrades.
Dev-only measurement probes published on window (e.g. __carFootprint, __roadCrossings) and stripped from production via process.env.NODE_ENV inlining. Useful for verifying 3D framing numerically.

HANDOVER traps to remember: reach the Next 16 dev server via `localhost`, not 127.0.0.1 (cross-origin dev resources are blocked and the bundle silently never boots; or set allowedDevOrigins). A hidden browser pane pauses rAF and React 19's Suspense reveal, so measure motion in a visible pane and wait for a native rAF before reading.
Native <dialog>.showModal() for every modal and drawer (real focus trap and inert background), body:has(dialog[open]) scroll lock, and closing on pathname change.
CRM design density spec (13px base, mono tabular numerics right-aligned, no zebra, 22px status chips with a dot, horizontal-only chart grid, no animation on filtered charts) reads as a serious tool.

Anti-template checklist from art-direction §8 maps directly onto ProDevly's 'no AI-generated themes' rule (no purple/blue gradient plus glass card, no icon-in-circle feature cards, no emoji, no rounded-everything, no star testimonials, no trust ribbons, ≤3 weights per viewport, house easing curves instead of default ease).
